title: Conexiom / Revere Electric case study
inspection: Vendor-authored deployment case, older/undated document; read background and solution/results portions
finding: An electrical distributor used order automation alongside Eclipse. It demonstrates adoption of this category, not our delivery performance or NetSuite compatibility.

title: Celigo: non-EDI order processing
inspection: Primary technical documentation, dated 19 October 2026; workflow and validation sections read
finding: Documents an existing email/file-to-ERP route with checks and exception handling. Important contrary evidence: the basic capability is already available; we sell scoped implementation, not invented technology.

title: Prokeep product
inspection: Primary product page; relevant product and demo text inspected
finding: Markets distributor order capture, quoting and ERP connections. Strong direct alternative; no claim that our concept has unique features.

title: Prokeep pricing
inspection: Primary pricing page; plans and implementation support portions read
finding: Pricing is custom and branch based. Order automation appears under Pro; vendor also provides implementation support. No numerical quote verified.

title: Celigo pricing
inspection: Primary pricing page; visible pricing principles and edition information inspected
finding: Account-specific licensing must be checked. No verified dollar price for the proposed configuration; do not treat the model allowance as a vendor quote.

title: Celigo integration partners
inspection: Primary partner page; programme and service descriptions read
finding: There is an established ecosystem selling integrations. This supports a delivery route, not evidence that a client will pay our proposed fee.

title: Wholesale ordering discussion
inspection: Anonymous buyer/practitioner discussion; original post and relevant replies inspected, not independently verified
finding: A poster describes manual NetSuite entry for small-retailer orders; a commenter describes improving a distributor workflow. Useful discovery language, not a measured market study.

title: Manual order-processing discussion
inspection: Anonymous thread; original post and early replies inspected; some replies suspect promotion
finding: Shows format/exception concerns, but also a counterexample: some orders are entered in only a few minutes. Weak corroboration; low-volume/fast-entry firms can be poor prospects.

title: QuoteWerks
inspection: Primary product page/search material; partial inspection only
finding: Alternative quoting tools exist for CRM/PSA/supplier workflows. Breadth scan only; no separate market recommendation.

title: BuildOps preventive maintenance
inspection: Primary product page; feature and result sections partially inspected
finding: Maintenance agreement operations and renewals are a native software category. Breadth scan, not a researched gap.

title: Bullhorn candidate re-engagement
finding: Basic candidate re-engagement already has a native recipe. It needs a stronger service case than setting up a sequence.

title: Front / Load One
inspection: Vendor case study; solution/API workflow portions read
finding: A freight operator connected email with its proprietary quoting workflow. Real implementation example reported by vendor; more integration dependencies than the selected bounded pilot.

title: Celigo / Call One
inspection: Vendor case study PDF; background and challenge inspected
finding: Telecom-products distributor needed to connect order/product workflows across systems. Product-feed opportunity remains a lightly scanned lead.
